issues.body: The new generator is optional, while `expected_records()` continues to accept the old `{"targets": ...}` shape without any generator provenance or other distinction. Consequently an operator can still pass a manually transcribed manifest that omits PRs, have `audit()` set `complete = True`, and receive revocation candidates. The added `[#1027] the TYPED manifest omitting PR 9...` assertion proves this exact unsafe path remains live: it expects `STATUS_SCOPED` and `[redacted-account]` as a candidate. Updating comments/help to say manifests are derived does not prevent the dangerous input from arming the result.
issues.fix_hint: Make the arm-side reader reject legacy/hand-written completeness claims, or otherwise cryptographically/structurally bind accepted manifests to a validated generation path. Add an end-to-end negative test showing that the short typed manifest used in the current #1027 fixture cannot produce `STATUS_SCOPED` or any revocation candidate. If legacy manifests must remain readable, ensure they are advisory-only and cannot set `complete` until converted through the trusted generation workflow.
issues.title: Hand-written short manifests remain arm-capable

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The generator is carefully implemented and its CLI/source-directory checks are meaningfully exercised, but it does not close the fail-open path the change says it closes. The audit still accepts an arbitrary hand-written short manifest, and the new self-test explicitly demonstrates that such a manifest marks a partial corpus scoped and proposes a false revocation. Because this is the trust decision the feature is meant to make safe, the change is incomplete.
